text:
Maya: Quick infra question — planning to move redwood-api svc from NodePort -> ClusterIP behind ALB ingress and terminate TLS at the ALB. Going to add cert ARN via Terraform. Anyone see immediate gotchas?

Eric: ALB ingress is fine for app HTTP, but remember ALB terminates TLS so pods will see plain HTTP. If you need client certs or mTLS, NLB passthrough is required.

Maya: Good call. We don’t need mTLS for this API. Main concerns: target-type=ip, health check path, security groups, and how we pull the cert ARN from secrets. I sketched the TF change below.

Maya: ```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener" "https" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.alb.arn
  port              = "443"
  protocol          = "HTTPS"
  ssl_policy        = "ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01"
  certificate_arn   = var.alb_certificate_arn
  default_action {
    type = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.app.arn
  }
}

resource "aws_lb_target_group" "app" {
  name     = "redwood-api-tg"
  port     = 80
  protocol = "HTTP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    path                = "/_hc"
    matcher             = "200-399"
    interval            = 15
    healthy_threshold   = 2
  }
}
```

Jonah: A few notes:
- Make sure the k8s Service uses port name like `http` (ALB uses port name to map protocols).
- Target group using IP is correct for pods.
- Health check path /_hc is okay but ensure pod returns 200 quickly.

Maya: Service manifest I'm planning:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: redwood-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: redwood-api
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
      name: http
```

Eric: Also add these ingress annotations for the AWS ALB ingress controller: `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-type: ip`, `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-path: /_hc`, and `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'`. And confirm the ingress controller IAM role can describe target groups.

Sean: Where are we storing the certificate ARN? Secrets Manager or SSM? For infra TF I prefer SSM parameter so non-privileged reviewers can see value is set but not the certificate contents.

Maya: We have existing pattern: store cert ARN in SSM parameter "/infra/certs/redwood-api-prod/arn". Terraform reads it via data aws_ssm_parameter. Snippet:```hcl
data "aws_ssm_parameter" "api_cert_arn" {
  name = "/infra/certs/redwood-api-prod/arn"
}
variable "alb_certificate_arn" {
  default = data.aws_ssm_parameter.api_cert_arn.value
}
```

Jonah: Also update the ALB SG to allow inbound 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 (or locked by WAF if needed) and ensure nodes' SG allows traffic from ALB SG on instance port 80. For EKS with ENI mode target IPs, the target SG must allow ALB.

Eric: One more: websocket endpoints — if redwood-api has socket endpoints, ALB supports websockets but you need proper idle timeouts. Default 60s may drop long-lived streams. Set `connection_draining`/`timeout` accordingly.

Maya: Noted, we do not use websockets here.

Maya: I'll open a PR to infra/ingress with the TF + k8s manifest updates and link the k8s change in the app repo. Planning to deploy to staging first. @Eric can you do a quick review of the TF bits? @Jonah can you sanity-check healthcheck behaviour in staging? :pray:

Eric: Yep I can review tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

Jonah: I'll run a canary in staging and test healthcheck/graceful termination.

infra-bot: Deployment job queued — infra/ingress#148 (staging) — started by Maya — build 1123. ETA ~4m

Maya: Thanks all. I'll include test checklist in the PR description (SG, TG health, logs, metrics).
